flashcards.concept_name: Svataḥ Prāmāṇyavāda vs. Parataḥ Prāmāṇyavāda

chain.from_concept: Cārvāka Skepticism (Doubt of all unperceived entities)
chain.current_thesis: Cognition carries its own truth at inception (Svataḥ), or requires external pragmatic verification (Parataḥ).
chain.to_concept: Theories of Illusion (If knowledge is self-valid, how does error occur? -> Khyātivāda)

flashcards.the_problem: Does a valid cognition (pramā) possess intrinsic validity from the very moment of its emergence, or must truth be proven by an external test?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Intrinsic validity; self-authentication of cognition in origin (utpattau) and apprehension (jñāptau).
Extrinsic validity; verified via causal excellence (guṇa) and successful action (pravṛtti-sāmarthya).
Infinite regress that occurs if every validating cognition itself needs validation.
Sublating cognition that cancels an erroneous perception.

dialectic.purvapaksha: The Nyāya argues: If all cognitions were intrinsically valid, doubts and illusions would never happen. A thirsty traveler sees a mirage; only reaching the pool and drinking (pravṛtti-sāmarthya) verifies the cognition as true.
dialectic.siddhanta: Kumārila Bhaṭṭa counters: If cognition A needs cognition B to validate it, and B needs C, knowledge never arrives at certainty (anavasthā). Cognition is born valid from its own apparatus; falsity alone is extrinsic, exposed by a defeater (bādhaka).

flashcards.interview_trap: Distinguish Bhāṭṭa from Prābhākara Mīmāṃsā: Bhāṭṭas hold that cognition is supersensuous and inferred from 'knownness' (jñātatā) in the object, whereas Prābhākaras reject jñātatā, argue for 'Tripuṭī-pratyakṣa' (simultaneous awareness of knower, known, knowing), and claim NO cognition is ever false (Akhyātivāda).
flashcards.wisdom_gist: At the root of thought lies a baseline epistemic trust. Without trusting our primary apprehension until contradicted, the human mind falls into paralyzing infinite regression.

flashcards.concept_name: Pratyakṣa: Nirvikalpaka vs. Savikalpaka & Ṣaḍvidha-Sannikarṣa

chain.from_concept: Svataḥ/Parataḥ Prāmāṇya (Establishing whether perception is self-certifying)
chain.current_thesis: Perception begins as non-judgmental bare awareness (nirvikalpaka) before structuring into relational conceptuality (savikalpaka) via 6 types of contact.
chain.to_concept: Buddhist Pramāṇavāda (Dignāga & Dharmakīrti rejecting Savikalpaka as pure conceptual fiction / Kalpanā)

flashcards.the_problem: How does sensory contact with an external object translate from a raw sensory datum into a structured, conceptual judgment ('This is a brown earthen pot')?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Indeterminate, non-propositional perception apprehending bare structure without name or genus.
Determinate, propositional perception grasping the object qualified by name, genus, and attribute (viśeṣya-viśeṣaṇa-sambandha).
The sixfold sense-object contacts: Saṃyoga, Saṃyukta-samavāya, Saṃyukta-samaveta-samavāya, Samavāya, Samaveta-samavāya, Viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣya-bhāva.
Extraordinary perception: Sāmānyalakṣaṇa (genus), Jñānalakṣaṇa (complication/memory), Yogaja (intuitive gnosis).

dialectic.purvapaksha: The Buddhist epistemologist (Dharmakīrti) argues: Perception is strictly non-conceptual (kalpanāpoḍham). The moment language, name, or universal is applied, it is no longer perception but mental construction (vikalpa). Savikalpaka is not perception at all.
dialectic.siddhanta: The Naiyāyika retorts: The universal (sāmānya) is a real objective entity inhering in the object. Savikalpaka perception directly sees the real substance as qualified by its real universal; words merely express what the sense faculty has already veridically grasped.

flashcards.interview_trap: How does Nyāya perceive absence (abhāva)? Through the 6th sannikarṣa: 'Viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣya-bhāva' (the absence of pot is an adjective qualifying the bare ground). Contrast this with Bhāṭṭa Mīmāṃsā, which invents a separate 6th pramāṇa: Anupalabdhi (non-apprehension).
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Human perception is never merely passive recording; our cognitive faculties instantly weave raw immediacy into an intelligible, structured reality of meaning.

flashcards.concept_name: Anumāna: The Pañcāvayava Syllogism & Vyāpti

chain.from_concept: Pratyakṣa (Perception is limited to present objects)
chain.current_thesis: Inference extends knowledge to unperceived realms through an unbroken invariant relation (Vyāpti) formulated in a five-membered syllogism.
chain.to_concept: Hetvābhāsa (The fallacies that rupture Vyāpti and corrupt inference)

flashcards.the_problem: How can the mind legitimately cross the gap between what is currently perceived (smoke on a mountain) and what is hidden from view (fire inside the mountain)?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Invariable, unconditional relation of concomitance between the sign (hetu/smoke) and the signified (sādhya/fire).
The 5 members of demonstration: Pratijñā (thesis), Hetu (reason), Udāharaṇa (universal exemplification), Upanaya (application), Nigamana (conclusion).
An extraneous condition that renders a concomitance conditional (e.g., 'wet fuel' is the upādhi for smoke from fire).
The synthetic cognitive act: realization that the mountain possesses smoke which is invariably accompanied by fire.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Cārvāka challenges: How do you know Vyāpti holds universally? You have seen fire with smoke in a kitchen, but have you seen every fire in all past, present, and future universes? If you infer it, you presuppose inference; induction is logically circular.
dialectic.siddhanta: Nyāya solves the Indian problem of induction through 'Sāmānyalakṣaṇa-pratyakṣa' (perceiving smokiness as a universal in all smoke) combined with 'Tarka' (reductio ad absurdum: 'If smoke could occur without fire, why does no one look for smoke in a lake?').

flashcards.interview_trap: Compare the Nyāya 5-membered syllogism with Aristotle's 3-membered syllogism: Aristotle's syllogism is purely deductive and formal; the Nyāya pañcāvayava is BOTH inductive and deductive, requiring an empirical example (Udāharaṇa) from the world.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Inference is the bridge between the finite senses and the infinite world. Reason does not float in formal abstraction; it remains anchored to lived empirical observation.

flashcards.concept_name: Hetvābhāsa: The Five Inferential Fallacies

chain.from_concept: Anumāna & Vyāpti (The criteria of valid inference)
chain.current_thesis: A pseudo-reason (hetvābhāsa) appears to establish a conclusion but violates one of the 5 conditions of a valid hetu (rūpa-pañcaka).
chain.to_concept: Debate Methodology (Vāda, Jalpa, Vitaṇḍā in Nyāya epistemology)

flashcards.the_problem: What precise logical defects destroy the validity of an inference, causing the reason (hetu) to yield error or contradiction?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The erratic/inconclusive reason: Sādhāraṇa (too wide), Asādhāraṇa (too narrow), Anupasaṃhārī (non-exclusive).
The contradictory reason: establishes the exact opposite of what was to be proved (e.g., 'Sound is eternal because it is produced').
The counterbalanced reason: an equally strong contrary inference exists against it.
The unproved/unfounded reason: Āśrayāsiddha (unreal subject), Svarūpāsiddha (absent in subject), Vyāpyatvāsiddha (conditional).
The sublated reason: the conclusion is directly contradicted by a stronger pramāṇa like perception ('Fire is cold because it is a substance').

dialectic.purvapaksha: Early thinkers wondered: Why are there 5 distinct fallacies rather than simply one overarching category of 'invalid inference'?
dialectic.siddhanta: Nyāya systematically deduces the 5 fallacies from the 5 essential characteristics of a sound reason (rūpa-pañcaka): (1) presence in pakṣa, (2) presence in sapakṣa, (3) absence in vipakṣa, (4) absence of counterbalancing reason, (5) non-sublation by perception. Each fallacy corresponds to the breakdown of one specific leg.

flashcards.interview_trap: What is the crucial difference between Satpratipakṣa and Bādhita? In Satpratipakṣa, the opposition is from another INFERENCE of equal strength; in Bādhita, the conclusion is cancelled by a non-inferential, immediate source like PERCEPTION (e.g., touch tells us fire is hot).
flashcards.wisdom_gist: A false reason does not merely fail to prove truth; it seduces the mind into dogmatism. Rigorous thinking begins by interrogating the unstated flaws in our own arguments before attacking others.

flashcards.concept_name: Satkāryavāda vs. Asatkāryavāda (Pariṇāmavāda vs. Ārambhavāda)

chain.from_concept: Epistemic validity of empirical observation (How objects change)
chain.current_thesis: The effect pre-exists in the material cause prior to production (Satkāryavāda), versus the effect is an entirely de novo creation (Asatkāryavāda).
chain.to_concept: Cosmic Evolution & Dissolution (Sāṃkhya's 24 Tattvas & Advaita's Vivartavāda)

flashcards.the_problem: Does change create something genuinely brand new out of non-being, or does change merely unveil what was already latently present in the cause?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The doctrine of existent effect: the effect is an unmanifest state of the cause.
Real transformation: the cause undergoes real ontological modification into the effect (Sāṃkhya).
The doctrine of fresh origination: the effect is non-existent before production (Nyāya).
Illusory modification: the cause appears as effect without undergoing change (Advaita Vedānta).

dialectic.purvapaksha: The Naiyāyika argues: If the cloth already existed inside the threads, the weaver's effort is pointless, and threads could clothe a shivering person. The cloth is a new substance inhering in threads.
dialectic.siddhanta: Īśvarakṛṣṇa in Sāṃkhyakārikā 9 proves Satkāryavāda: (1) Asadakaraṇāt (oil cannot be pressed from sand), (2) Upādānagrahaṇāt (specific materials needed for specific effects), (3) Sarvasambhavābhāvāt (not everything from anything), (4) Śaktasya śakyakaraṇāt (cause produces only what it has potential for), (5) Kāraṇabhāvāt (cause and effect share essence).

flashcards.interview_trap: Both Sāṃkhya and Advaita accept Satkāryavāda, but differ radically on transformation: Sāṃkhya asserts PARIṆĀMA (real, physical evolution of Prakṛti), while Advaita asserts VIVARTA (apparent, illusory superimposition on unchanging Brahman).
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Nothing emerges out of sheer void. Creativity is not ex nihilo creation; it is the patient unfolding of inherent potentiality into vivid actuality.

flashcards.concept_name: Adhyāsa, Māyā & The Two Tiers of Reality

chain.from_concept: Vivartavāda (The effect as an appearance of the cause)
chain.current_thesis: The perceived diversity of the universe is a superimposition (Adhyāsa) upon pure non-dual consciousness (Brahman) via inexplicable ignorance (Māyā/Avidyā).
chain.to_concept: Rāmānuja's Critique of Advaita (The Saptavidhā Anupapatti)

flashcards.the_problem: How can the pure, undivided, immutable Brahman appear as a cosmos of suffering, multiplicity, and individual bound souls (jīvas)?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Superimposition: the apparent presentation of an attribute of one thing onto another (smṛtirūpaḥ paratra pūrvadṛṣṭāvabhāsaḥ).
The cosmic principle of illusion possessing two powers: Āvaraṇa (veiling reality) and Vikṣepa (projecting multiplicity).
Three tiers of reality: Pāramārthika (Absolute/Brahman), Vyāvahārika (Empirical/World), Prātibhāsika (Illusory/Dreams).
The witness-consciousness that illuminates both knowledge and ignorance without participating in action.

dialectic.purvapaksha: The realist asks: The subject (knower) and object (known) are as opposed as light and darkness. How can the attributes of the insentient world be superimposed upon the pure conscious self?
dialectic.siddhanta: Śaṅkara opens the Brahmasūtra-Bhāṣya by declaring Adhyāsa natural and beginningless (naisargiko 'yaṃ lokavyavahāraḥ). Just as a blameless sky appears blue or contaminated by dust, consciousness misidentifies with body and mind due to innate nescience.

flashcards.interview_trap: Did Śaṅkara claim the world is a complete hallucination like a dream? NO! That is the trap. Śaṅkara vigorously refutes Buddhist subjective idealism (Yogācāra) in BS 2.2.28; the empirical world possesses Vyāvahārika Sattā (objective reality for all practical purposes) until sublated by Brahman-knowledge.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Much of our anxiety and suffering stems from superimposing ephemeral psychological identities onto the silent, untroubled witness within.

flashcards.concept_name: Rāmānuja's Aprathaksiddhi & Saptavidhā Anupapatti

chain.from_concept: Advaita's Nirguṇa Brahman & Māyāvāda
chain.current_thesis: Brahman is organically qualified by real matter (acit) and real souls (cit) through inseparability (Aprathaksiddhi); Māyā is logically self-contradictory in 7 ways.
chain.to_concept: Dvaita Vedānta (Madhva's rejection of all non-difference in favor of Pañca-bheda)

flashcards.the_problem: Can non-dualism preserve the reality of individual souls, the external cosmos, and personal devotion (Bhakti) without dismissing them as illusory nescience?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Inseparable relation: mode cannot exist without substance, yet is distinct from it (unlike Nyāya's Samavāya).
Body-Soul analogy: the world and individual souls constitute the real body (śarīra) of God (Brahman).
Rāmānuja's 7 great incoherences of Advaita's Māyā: Āśraya, Tirodhāna, Svarūpa, Anirvacanīya, Pramāṇa, Nivartaka, Nivṛtti.
Non-duality of the qualified whole; Brahman qualified by subtle souls/matter becomes Brahman qualified by gross souls/matter.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Śaṅkara argued that all differentiation is illusory; pure Nirguṇa Brahman alone is real, and any quality implies finitude.
dialectic.siddhanta: Rāmānuja in Śrībhāṣya dismantles Māyā: (1) Where does Māyā reside (Āśrayānupapatti)? Not in Brahman (pure light cannot host darkness) and not in Jīva (Jīva is produced by Māyā—circular reasoning!). (2) How can it veil self-luminous Brahman (Tirodhānānupapatti)? Veiling luminosity destroys its nature. Brahman is SAGUṆA, adorned with infinite auspicious qualities (kalyāṇa-guṇas).

primary_text.author: Rāmānuja
primary_text.passage: Introduction to BS 1.1.1 (The Great Siddhānta / Mahā-siddhānta)

flashcards.interview_trap: Compare Aprathaksiddhi (Viśiṣṭādvaita) and Samavāya (Nyāya): Samavāya relates two ALREADY established separate substances (ayutasiddha); Aprathaksiddhi relates an attribute that CANNOT even be conceived or exist without its substantive substrate.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: The universe is not an empty illusion to be escaped; it is the living, breathing body of the Divine, worthy of reverence, care, and loving devotion.

flashcards.concept_name: Pratītyasamutpāda and Nāgārjuna's Śūnyatā

chain.from_concept: Abhidharma atomism (Searching for irreducible svabhāva in dharmas)
chain.current_thesis: Whatever is dependently co-arisen is devoid of inherent essence (Śūnyatā); emptiness is not nothingness, but the condition for all change and awakening.
chain.to_concept: Yogācāra Vijñaptimātratā (Reconstructing the mind from the ashes of extreme deconstruction)

flashcards.the_problem: If all phenomena arise dependently upon causes and conditions, can any entity possess independent, immutable essence (svabhāva)?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Dependent co-arising: nothing exists uncaused, isolated, or self-grounded.
Emptiness; absence of fixed, self-sufficient inherent nature (niḥsvabhāvatā).
Four-cornered dialectic: It is not A, not non-A, not both, not neither.
The total relinquishing of all dogmatic philosophical viewpoints.

dialectic.purvapaksha: The realist objects: If all dharmas are empty, morality, the Four Noble Truths, and liberation become fictions. Emptiness leads to terrifying nihilism (ucchedavāda).
dialectic.siddhanta: Nāgārjuna turns the table in MMK 24.18: If things had fixed svabhāva, they could NEVER change! A seed could never sprout; a bound person could never achieve liberation. It is precisely because everything is empty that causal transformation and spiritual freedom are possible.

flashcards.interview_trap: Never equate Śūnyatā with nothingness (abhāva)! Nāgārjuna warns in MMK 24.11: 'A wrongly grasped emptiness ruins a person of little intelligence, like a snake handled carelessly or a magic spell misapplied!'
flashcards.wisdom_gist: To be empty is not to be nothing; it is to be open to everything. Letting go of rigid identities reveals that life's interdependency is the foundation of compassion.

flashcards.concept_name: Anekāntavāda, Syādvāda & Nayavāda

chain.from_concept: Dogmatic absolutisms (Advaita's eternal permanence vs Buddhism's flux)
chain.current_thesis: Reality is multifaceted and complex (Anekānta); every predication must be conditional and standpoint-relative (Syādvāda).
chain.to_concept: Jaina Ethics: Ahiṃsā as the intellectual duty of respecting rival philosophical perspectives

flashcards.the_problem: How can philosophy overcome the dogmatic clashes between systems that assert reality is purely permanent (Vedānta) and systems that assert it is purely momentary (Buddhism)?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Metaphysical doctrine of non-one-sidedness: reality possesses infinite attributes (ananta-dharmātmakam vastu).
Epistemological doctrine of conditional predication: using 'Syāt' (in some respect) to avoid dogmatism.
Seven-fold predication: syād asti, syān nāsti, syād asti nāsti ca, syād avaktavyaḥ, etc.
Theory of partial standpoints: examining reality through specialized perspectives (e.g., Dravyārthika vs Paryāyārthika naya).

dialectic.purvapaksha: Śaṅkara and the Naiyāyikas attack: Syādvāda is sheer nonsense. A thing cannot be both hot and cold at the same time; qualifying everything with 'somehow' violates the law of contradiction.
dialectic.siddhanta: The Jaina answers: It is not in the SAME respect that a thing is and is not! A gold ring IS from the standpoint of substance (gold), but IS NOT from the standpoint of previous form (necklace). Absolute permanent vs absolute momentary are one-sided abstractions (ekāntas). Reality is Dravya-Guṇa-Paryāya (substance with enduring qualities undergoing modes).

primary_text.author: Mallisena & Kundakunda
primary_text.passage: Syādvādamañjarī on Kārikā 28; Pravacanasāra Book II

flashcards.interview_trap: Understand why 'Avaktavya' (inexpressible) is the 4th step in Saptabhaṅgī: It occurs when one attempts to state existence and non-existence SIMULTANEOUSLY (yugapat), which language cannot do. Contrast with the 3rd step which states them sequentially (kramaśaḥ).
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Intellectual humility is the highest form of non-violence. Recognizing that our personal viewpoint captures only one facet of the infinite jewel of reality disarms dogmatism.

flashcards.concept_name: Descartes' Method of Doubt & The Cogito

chain.from_concept: Medieval Scholastic Dogmatism & Montaigne's Skepticism
chain.current_thesis: By pushing doubt to its hyper-radical limit (evil demon), the indubitable bedrock of the thinking self (Cogito) is discovered.
chain.to_concept: Cartesian Dualism & The Mind-Body Interaction Problem (Spinoza's Monism)

flashcards.the_problem: How can human cognition discover an indubitable, rock-solid foundation for knowledge that withstands all skeptical assault?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Systematic suspension of assent to any belief that admits of the slightest uncertainty.
The ultimate skeptical thought experiment: an all-powerful deceiver manipulating math and sensory perceptions.
I think, therefore I am; the self-authenticating certainty that doubt requires a doubter.
Substance dualism: thinking unextended substance (mind) vs unthinking extended substance (matter).

dialectic.purvapaksha: The radical skeptic asserts: We cannot trust our senses (dreams deceive us) and we cannot trust mathematics (a malicious demon could deceive us every time we add 2 and 3). Knowledge is impossible.
dialectic.siddhanta: Descartes points out in Meditation II: Let the demon deceive me as much as he can, he can NEVER bring it about that I am nothing so long as I think that I am something. Even to be deceived, I must exist. Cogito is self-verifying.

flashcards.interview_trap: Did Descartes mean 'I think, therefore I am' as a syllogistic inference with a hidden major premise ('Whatever thinks exists')? NO! Descartes clarifies in the Second Replies that the Cogito is a direct, immediate intellectual intuition, not a syllogism.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Even in the deepest crisis of doubt, consciousness discovers its own indomitable presence. The capacity to question is proof of our being.

flashcards.concept_name: Locke's Tabula Rasa & Primary vs. Secondary Qualities

chain.from_concept: Cartesian Innate Ideas (Descartes & Leibniz)
chain.current_thesis: The mind is a blank slate (Tabula Rasa) furnished entirely by experience; reality splits into objective primary and subjective secondary qualities.
chain.to_concept: Berkeley's Immaterialism (Dissolving primary qualities into secondary ones: Esse est percipi)

flashcards.the_problem: Where do our ideas come from if there are no innate truths stamped on the human soul at birth?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The mind initially devoid of all characters, filled solely through Sensation and Reflection.
Qualities inseparable from matter that resemble our ideas: extension, figure, motion, rest, solidity.
Powers in objects to produce sensations in us via primary qualities: colors, sounds, tastes, odors.
The obscure unknown substrate required to support qualities.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Rationalists argued that universal principles of logic (the law of identity) and moral ideas must be innate because children and animals cannot extract necessity from messy sensory instances.
dialectic.siddhanta: Locke in Book I of the Essay demonstrates that children and idiots do NOT possess the law of non-contradiction! If an idea were innate, it would be universally conscious. All complex ideas are constructed from simple ideas of sensation and internal reflection.

primary_text.author: John Locke
primary_text.passage: Book I, Chapters 1–2; Book II, Chapter 8 (§§ 9–26)

flashcards.interview_trap: Interview boards frequently ask: 'What was Locke's test for distinguishing primary from secondary qualities?' Primary qualities survive physical division (divide a grain of wheat in half, each piece retains extension and solidity); secondary qualities change or vanish (almonds pounded in a mortar lose their color and texture).
flashcards.wisdom_gist: We enter the world with minds open and ready to learn. Experience is the great teacher, and knowledge is built through patient, honest sensory engagement.

flashcards.concept_name: Berkeley's Esse est Percipi & Immaterialism

chain.from_concept: Locke's Primary vs Secondary Qualities & Material Substance
chain.current_thesis: Matter does not exist; to be is to be perceived (Esse est percipi) or to perceive (Esse est percipere).
chain.to_concept: Hume's Radical Skepticism (Applying Berkeley's critique to mental substance itself)

flashcards.the_problem: If secondary qualities exist only in the mind, how can primary qualities (shape, size) exist in an unthinking, unperceived 'material substance' outside mind?

technical_lexicon.meaning: To be is to be perceived: sensible things are collections of ideas in minds.
Can you conceive of a tree existing unperceived? The moment you conceive it, you are perceiving it in thought; unperceived matter is an impossibility.
The rejection of inert matter; reality consists of minds (spirits) and their ideas.
Things don't vanish when we leave the room because God's omnipresent mind perceives the universe continuously.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Locke and common sense argue: Even if color is subjective, the table's shape and solidity belong to the real physical object behind the sensory veil.
dialectic.siddhanta: Berkeley retorts: Try conceiving extension without color or texture! You cannot. Extension is known ONLY through visual or tactile sensations. If secondary qualities are mind-dependent, primary qualities must be equally mind-dependent. 'Material substance' is an incoherent philosophical phantom.

primary_text.author: George Berkeley
primary_text.work: A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge

flashcards.interview_trap: Did Berkeley deny the reality of the physical world? Berkeley insisted he was defending common sense against skeptical materialists! He never denied that apples are crisp and stones hard; he only denied that they are made of unperceivable 'matter'. They are real, regular ideas caused by God.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: The world is not a cold machine of dead matter spinning in empty space. Reality is an ongoing, luminous conversation between consciousness and creation.

flashcards.concept_name: Hume's Problem of Induction & The Critique of Necessary Connection

chain.from_concept: Rationalist Causal Metaphysics & Empiricist Association
chain.current_thesis: Causation has no observable necessity; induction is grounded not in reason, but in psychological custom (habit).
chain.to_concept: Kant's Awakening from Dogmatic Slumber (The Synthetic A Priori)

flashcards.the_problem: Can we logically demonstrate that the future will resemble the past, or that causes contain a necessary power to produce their effects?

technical_lexicon.meaning: All inquiries divided into Relations of Ideas (analytic/a priori) and Matters of Fact (synthetic/a posteriori).
Repeated observation of event B following event A in time and space, without any visible tie of necessity.
The psychological instinct that leads animals and humans to expect like effects from like causes.
The inductive presupposition that nature behaves uniformly, which cannot be proved without circularity.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Descartes and Spinoza asserted that causes necessarily contain their effects with mathematical certainty discoverable by intellect.
dialectic.siddhanta: Hume demonstrates in Section IV of the Enquiry: Inspect a billiard ball striking another. You see movement, contact, and the second ball rolling. You NEVER perceive the 'power' or 'necessary connection'. Attempting to prove induction by induction is circular reasoning (begging the question).

flashcards.interview_trap: Selection committees love to ask: 'Did Hume advise abandoning science and causal expectations?' Hume answered NO! Skeptical doubt shows the limits of theoretical reason, but practical life must follow natural instinct: 'Be a philosopher; but, amidst all your philosophy, be still a man.'
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Intellectual pride claims universal certitude, but philosophical wisdom recognizes that our deepest expectations rest on the humble habits of nature.

flashcards.concept_name: Kant's Synthetic A Priori & Transcendental Deduction

chain.from_concept: Hume's Inductive Skepticism (Awakening Kant from dogmatic slumber)
chain.current_thesis: Knowledge of the empirical world requires synthetic a priori concepts (categories) that structure the raw sensory manifold into knowable experience.
chain.to_concept: Hegel's Dialectic (Overcoming Kant's rigid barrier between phenomena and noumena)

flashcards.the_problem: How can science possess universal, necessary laws (like causality and mathematics) if all empirical knowledge is contingent?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Objects conform to the cognitive structure of the human mind, rather than the mind conforming to objects.
Judgments that expand knowledge (synthetic) yet hold with strict universality and necessity (a priori).
Space and Time as the pure a priori subjective lenses of sensory receptivity.
The 'I think' that must be able to accompany all representations to make experience unified.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Hume argued causality is just an empirical association of ideas, leaving science without necessary foundation.
dialectic.siddhanta: Kant proves in the Critique of Pure Reason: Causality is not an empirical discovery from experience; it is a CATEGORY of the understanding that makes experience possible in the first place! Without categories, sensory input would be a blind, chaotic blur.

primary_text.author: Immanuel Kant
primary_text.work: Critique of Pure Reason (Kritik der reinen Vernunft)

flashcards.interview_trap: Can we know the 'Ding an sich' (Thing-in-itself)? A decisive NO! Kant limits synthetic a priori knowledge strictly to PHENOMENA (appearances). Reason attempting to know the unconditioned noumenon falls into inescapable Antinomies.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: The human mind does not passively reflect the universe; it actively gives order, continuity, and intelligibility to the world we inhabit.

flashcards.concept_name: Husserl's Epoché & Intentionality

chain.from_concept: 19th Century Psychologism & Uncritical Naturalism
chain.current_thesis: By bracketing belief in the external world (Epoché), consciousness reveals its essential intentional structure (consciousness-of).
chain.to_concept: Heidegger's Being and Time (Rejection of pure detached consciousness in favor of Dasein's Being-in-the-world)

flashcards.the_problem: How can philosophy become a rigorous, presuppositionless science grounded in things as they present themselves, rather than theoretical dogmas?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Suspending the 'natural attitude' (belief in the independent existence of the external world).
The defining property of mental acts: all consciousness is directed toward an object (consciousness-of something).
The subjective act of experiencing (noesis) vs the objective meaning-content experienced (noema).
Varying representations in imagination to intuit their invariant essences (Wesen).

dialectic.purvapaksha: Naturalists and psychologists claimed thoughts are merely neuro-physiological events in the brain caused by physical stimuli.
dialectic.siddhanta: Husserl demonstrates in Logical Investigations and Ideas I that logical truths (like 2+2=4) are not psychological brain events; they possess objective ideal validity. By performing the Epoché, we don't destroy the world; we bracket it to study the pure structures of meaning in consciousness.

primary_text.author: Edmund Husserl
primary_text.work: Ideas Pertaining to a Pure Phenomenology (Ideen I)

flashcards.interview_trap: Does the Epoché mean skepticism or solipsism? NO! Husserl explicitly warns that bracketing the natural attitude does not mean doubting or denying the world; it means putting its dogmatic metaphysical status 'out of play' (außer Aktion) to inspect how meaning is constituted.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Before we rush to explain the world with scientific theories, we must first learn to look with clear, unprejudiced eyes at how reality actually appears to lived awareness.

flashcards.concept_name: Heidegger's Dasein, Being-in-the-world & Zuhandenheit

chain.from_concept: Husserl's Detached Phenomenological Observer & Cartesian Dualism
chain.current_thesis: Human existence (Dasein) is not a detached subject looking at objects, but practical immersion (Being-in-the-world) dealing with equipment (ready-to-hand).
chain.to_concept: Sartre's Radical Freedom & Bad Faith (Being and Nothingness)

flashcards.the_problem: Why has Western metaphysics forgotten the fundamental question of Being (Seinsvergessenheit), reducing reality to inert, detached substances?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The human entity for whom its very Being is an issue; characterized by openness, thrownness, and care.
The primordial holistic involvement with the world prior to any subject-object split.
The practical familiarity of tools in use (the hammer) before they break.
Detached, theoretical contemplation of an object when practical activity breaks down.
Confronting one's non-relational finitude to break free from the conformist herd (das Man).

dialectic.purvapaksha: Descartes and traditional epistemologists began with an isolated ego thinking in an ivory tower, wondering if the external table is real.
dialectic.siddhanta: Heidegger proves in Sein und Zeit (1927): We do not encounter things as theoretical substances first! We encounter them practically in a workshop of significance. The carpenter doesn't contemplate the hammer; he hammers! Theoretical Cartesian detachment is a secondary breakdown of practical care (Sorge).

primary_text.author: Martin Heidegger
primary_text.passage: Division I (§§ 14–18 on Worldhood and Equipment) and Division II (§§ 46–53 on Death)

flashcards.interview_trap: Distinguish Husserl from Heidegger on method: Husserl uses the Epoché to step back into transcendental consciousness; Heidegger rejects this as impossible because Dasein is always already 'thrown' (Geworfen) into a concrete, historical language and world (Hermeneutic Phenomenology).
flashcards.wisdom_gist: We do not live inside our heads peering out through glass windows at an alien cosmos. We are deeply woven into the world. To live authentically is to own our finitude before time slips away.

flashcards.concept_name: Sartre: Existence Precedes Essence & Bad Faith

chain.from_concept: Heidegger's Thrownness (Geworfenheit) & Dasein's Finitude
chain.current_thesis: Human beings have no predetermined essence; we first exist, act, and define ourselves, condemned to be absolutely free.
chain.to_concept: Postmodern Critiques of Subjectivity (Foucault's Death of Man & Power)

flashcards.the_problem: If God does not exist to design human nature like a craftsman designs a paper-knife, what grounds moral responsibility and human identity?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Humans first encounter themselves in the world, and only through choices define who they are.
Non-conscious, solid, inert objects with fixed essences (a rock, a table).
Consciousness characterized by lack, temporality, and radical freedom.
Inauthenticity: lying to oneself by pretending to be a fixed object (en-soi) to evade the anguish of freedom.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Religious and biological essentialists assert that human nature is predetermined by divine commandment, genetic makeup, or societal roles.
dialectic.siddhanta: Sartre declares in Being and Nothingness: 'Man is condemned to be free.' A waiter playing the role of a waiter too enthusiastically is acting in Bad Faith—pretending his career is an inescapable physical essence like the solidity of a rock. We are entirely responsible for our choices.

primary_text.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
primary_text.work: Being and Nothingness (L'Être et le Néant)
primary_text.passage: Part I, Chapter 2 ('Bad Faith') & 'Existentialism is a Humanism' (1946)

flashcards.interview_trap: What is the crucial paradox of Bad Faith? In Bad Faith, the deceiver and the deceived are the EXACT SAME PERSON. It is not an ordinary lie told to others; it is consciousness using its own freedom to pretend it has no freedom.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: There are no ready-made excuses. We cannot blame our past, our parents, or our circumstances for our character. Every morning, life asks us: who will you choose to be today?

flashcards.concept_name: Sri Aurobindo: Involution-Evolution & The Supermind

chain.from_concept: Śaṅkara's Illusionist Māyāvāda vs Western Darwinian Materialism
chain.current_thesis: Matter is involved Spirit; cosmic evolution is the progressive ascent from Matter to Life, Mind, and Supramental Divine Gnosis.
chain.to_concept: Teilhard de Chardin's Omega Point & Modern Transhumanist Philosophy

flashcards.the_problem: Can spiritual liberation be reconciled with terrestrial life and cosmic evolution without dismissing the world as an illusion or reducing mind to dead matter?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The prior descent and self-concealment of Spirit (Saccidānanda) into the density of inert Matter.
The progressive ascent of consciousness unfolding what was secretly involved.
The intermediate divine gnosis linking transcendent Saccidānanda with the manifested cosmos.
Transformation of earthly human nature and divinization of life, rather than world-flight.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Traditional ascetic Vedānta claimed the world is a dream to be abandoned (Māyāvāda), while Darwinian science claimed evolution is accidental, blind, and physical.
dialectic.siddhanta: Aurobindo proclaims: 'Evolution is an inverse action of the involution.' Life cannot evolve out of matter unless it was already involved within it; mind cannot evolve from life unless already hidden therein. The world is the delightful play (Līlā) of the Spirit ascending toward divine embodiment.

primary_text.author: Sri Aurobindo
primary_text.passage: Book I, Chapters 1–4 & Chapter 14 ('The Supermind as Creator')

flashcards.interview_trap: Distinguish Aurobindo's evolution from Bergson's 'Élan Vital': Bergson's creative evolution is open-ended and non-teleological; Aurobindo's evolution is teleological and spiritual, anchored in the pre-existent descent (involution) of Saccidānanda.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: The human intellect is not the ultimate peak of evolution, but an intermediate transitional instrument. The universe is slowly awakening to its divine source through us.

flashcards.concept_name: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar: Navayāna & Annihilation of Caste

chain.from_concept: Orthodox Brahmanical Caste Sanctions & Hierarchical Dharma
chain.current_thesis: Religion must be reconstructed on universal human dignity, liberty, equality, and fraternity; caste is a graded inequality that destroys fraternity.
chain.to_concept: Constitutional Morality & Secular Democracy in Modern India

flashcards.the_problem: Can a religion remain valid if it sanctifies hereditary, graded inequality, and how does the rational reconstruction of Dhamma restore human dignity?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Rationalist, humanist Buddhism oriented toward social justice and liberation from caste oppression.
An ascending scale of reverence and descending scale of contempt, preventing collective revolt.
Dhamma is social morality and universal compassion (karuṇā/maitrī); Brahmanical Dharma is ritual law.
Paramount devotion to democratic procedure, secular equality, and legal rights over sectarian dogma.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Orthodox defenders claimed caste was divinely ordained by Puruṣa Sūkta (Ṛgveda 10.90) and justified by retributive past karma.
dialectic.siddhanta: Ambedkar in Annihilation of Caste and The Buddha and His Dhamma argued: 'Caste is not merely a division of labour; it is a division of labourers.' Any religion that denies human equality is an engine of oppression. True religion is morality that fosters fraternity among living human beings on this earth.

primary_text.author: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
primary_text.work: The Buddha and His Dhamma (1957) & Annihilation of Caste (1936)
primary_text.passage: The Buddha and His Dhamma, Book II, Part II ('Dhamma is Morality'); Annihilation of Caste §§ 14–20

flashcards.interview_trap: What was Ambedkar's critique of the Buddhist Four Noble Truths? Ambedkar rejected the orthodox interpretation of 'Sarvaṃ Duḥkham' as pessimistic metaphysical inevitability; he insisted socio-economic, human-inflicted suffering must be distinguished from existential sorrow, and the Sangha must model equality.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Philosophy cannot remain detached in ivory towers while human beings are humiliated. The true test of any philosophical vision is its power to dismantle cruelty and cultivate fraternity.

flashcards.concept_name: Swami Vivekananda: Practical Vedānta & Universal Religion

chain.from_concept: Medieval World-Renouncing Monasticism
chain.current_thesis: Advaitic oneness must not remain in mountain caves; it must be applied practically to uplift humanity through service to Daridra Nārāyaṇa.
chain.to_concept: Sri Aurobindo's Integral Yoga & Modern Engaged Vedānta

flashcards.the_problem: How can the supreme philosophical truth of Advaita (oneness of Brahman) be translated into social action, moral courage, and global religious harmony?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The application of non-dual spiritual realization to everyday social, educational, and ethical life.
Serving the suffering and downtrodden as direct worship of the living Divine.
Harmony of all faiths as different paths ascending the same spiritual mountain, avoiding dogmatism.
A balanced, scientific synthesis of intellect, devotion, action, and psychological meditation.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Critics claimed Vedānta fosters quietism, fatalism, and social passivity because it treats the world as an illusion.
dialectic.siddhanta: Vivekananda roared at the Parliament of Religions (1893) and in his London lectures: 'If you cannot worship your brother man, the manifested God, how can you worship an unmanifested God?' If all souls are Brahman, all human beings are inherently divine and equal. Service is not condescending charity; it is self-worship.

primary_text.author: Swami Vivekananda
primary_text.passage: Volume II: 'Practical Vedānta' (Lectures delivered in London, November 1896)

flashcards.interview_trap: Central University boards frequently ask: 'How does Vivekananda's concept of Maya differ from Shankara's?' Vivekananda did NOT treat Maya as an ontological illusion or theory; he called Maya 'a simple statement of fact of what we are and what we see around us'—the inescapable contradiction between the ideal and the real.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Strength is life; weakness is death. True spirituality is not running away from the world, but bringing the light of the divine into the dark corners of human suffering.

flashcards.concept_name: M. K. Gandhi: Satyāgraha, Ahiṃsā & Truth as God

chain.from_concept: Machiavellian Political Realism (Ends justify the means)
chain.current_thesis: Means and ends are convertible; Truth (Satya) is God, and Non-violence (Ahiṃsā) is the only means to realize it.
chain.to_concept: Contemporary Civil Rights Movements (Martin Luther King Jr. & Nelson Mandela)

flashcards.the_problem: Can politics and moral resistance be conducted without hatred, violence, and the utilitarian sacrifice of moral purity?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Soul-force or holding firmly to Truth; active non-violent resistance through self-suffering.
Active love and complete absence of ill-will in thought, word, and deed, even toward an oppressor.
The welfare and upliftment of all, prioritizing the last and least person (Antyodaya).
True self-rule: mastery over one's own desires and senses, beyond mere political transfer of power.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Political pragmatists argued that non-violence is the weapon of the weak and helpless, utterly ineffective against ruthless imperial powers.
dialectic.siddhanta: Gandhi insisted in Hind Swaraj: Ahiṃsā is the weapon of the supremely brave! Striking an opponent is easy and animalistic; absorbing blows without retaliating or hating requires immense spiritual fortitude. By appealing to the opponent's conscience through self-suffering (tapasya), Satyāgraha converts rather than destroys.

primary_text.author: Mahatma Gandhi
primary_text.passage: Hind Swaraj, Chapters 16 & 17 ('Brute Force' vs 'Soul Force')

flashcards.interview_trap: Notice Gandhi's crucial shift in formulation: Early in life, he stated 'God is Truth'; later (1929), he radically reversed it to 'TRUTH IS GOD'. Why? Because even an atheist seeks truth; by defining Truth as God, no sincere seeker of truth is excluded.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: The means are like the seed, and the end is like the tree. We cannot harvest peace by sowing seeds of bitterness and violence.

flashcards.concept_name: Madhvācārya: Pañca-Bheda & Svatantra-Asvatantra Tattva

chain.from_concept: Śaṅkara's Non-Dualism & Rāmānuja's Qualified Non-Dualism
chain.current_thesis: Reality is governed by five absolute, eternal, unbridgeable differences (Pañca-Bheda); God alone is independent.
chain.to_concept: Bhakti & Eternal Predestination (Tāratamya)

flashcards.the_problem: Can scriptural assertions of difference between the finite soul and the infinite God be taken literally without being dissolved into non-dualism?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Five eternal differences: God-Soul, God-Matter, Soul-Soul, Soul-Matter, Matter-Matter.
The sole Independent Reality (Viṣṇu) vs Dependent Realities (souls and world).
Internal differentiating power that accounts for distinction without multiplying substances.
Soul is an eternal reflection of God, distinct yet totally dependent.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Advaita claims 'Tat Tvam Asi' (Thou Art That) teaches non-dual identity between Jīva and Brahman.
dialectic.siddhanta: Madhva reads the Chāndogya text as 'Atat Tvam Asi' (Thou art NOT that!) or interprets it as similarity in essence. Perception and scripture everywhere confirm difference. Difference (Bheda) is the constitutional nature of reality (svarūpa-bheda).

primary_text.author: Madhvācārya
primary_text.passage: Section on the five eternal differences (Pañca-bheda)

flashcards.interview_trap: How does Madhva explain the relation between God and His qualities without multiplying entities? Madhva introduces 'Viśeṣa'—an internal differentiator that functions in place of difference without being an independent entity.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Acknowledging our finitude and honoring the reality of the other is not spiritual defeat; it is the humble foundation of reverence, gratitude, and devotion.

flashcards.concept_name: Patañjali: Citta-Vṛtti-Nirodha & Aṣṭāṅga Yoga

chain.from_concept: Sāṃkhya Metaphysical Discrimination (Viveka-khyāti)
chain.current_thesis: Liberation requires the practical cessation of mental fluctuations (citta-vṛtti-nirodha) through an eight-limbed methodology.
chain.to_concept: Kaivalya (Absolute isolation of pure consciousness / Puruṣa from Prakṛti)

flashcards.the_problem: How can consciousness free itself from the continuous psychological turbulence and false identification with mental states?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The cessation of the modifications/fluctuations of the mind-stuff.
The five afflictions: Avidyā (ignorance), Asmitā (egoism), Rāga (attachment), Dveṣa (aversion), Abhiniveśa (fear of death).
Eight limbs: Yama, Niyama, Āsana, Prāṇāyāma, Pratyāhāra, Dhāraṇā, Dhyāna, Samādhi.
Cognitive absorption (with seed) vs Supracognitive absorption (seedless/nirbīja).

dialectic.purvapaksha: Can the mind be quieted by intellectual knowledge alone, as Sāṃkhya suggests?
dialectic.siddhanta: Patañjali emphasizes in YS 1.2 and 1.12 that mere philosophical reflection cannot halt subconscious impressions (saṃskāras). Cessation requires systematic 'Abhyāsa' (repeated practice) and 'Vairāgya' (dispassion), culminating in stilling the mental vortex.

flashcards.interview_trap: What is the precise role of God (Īśvara) in Patañjali's Yoga compared to Nyāya? In Nyāya, God is the efficient creator of the universe; in Yoga, Īśvara is NOT a creator, but a special Puruṣa untouched by afflictions, serving as an optional object of meditation (Īśvara-praṇidhāna).
flashcards.wisdom_gist: When the churning waters of the lake grow still, the pebbles at the bottom become visible. Stilling mental turbulence reveals the quiet, untroubled luminosity of consciousness.

flashcards.concept_name: Cārvāka: Dehātmavāda & The Emergence of Consciousness

chain.from_concept: Vedic Sacrificialism & Post-Mortem Escapism
chain.current_thesis: Consciousness is an emergent property of the four physical elements; there is no soul, afterlife, or transcendent realm.
chain.to_concept: Epistemic Positivism & The Indian Problem of Induction

flashcards.the_problem: Can consciousness and psychological experience be fully accounted for without positing an eternal, non-physical soul entity?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The body itself is the self; consciousness is an attribute of the physical body.
Just as intoxicating power emerges from yeast and molasses, consciousness emerges from physical elements.
Only 4 elements are real: Earth, Water, Fire, Air (rejecting unperceived Space/Ākāśa).
Kāma (pleasure) is the only rational Puruṣārtha; virtue and wealth are mere instrumental means.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Realists argue: Consciousness cannot emerge from insentient matter! If matter had consciousness, a dead corpse would also be conscious.
dialectic.siddhanta: Cārvāka retorts in Sarvadarśanasaṃgraha: Intoxication is absent in individual ingredients, yet emerges when combined in specific organic proportions. A dead body lacks the vital breath and organic integration. 'I am fat, I am thin'—ordinary linguistic usage proves the self is the living body, nothing more.

flashcards.interview_trap: Did Cārvāka accept Ākāśa (Ether/Space) as an element? NO! Because space is not directly perceived by the senses, Cārvāka accepts only 4 elements (pṛthivī, ap, tejas, vāyu). Another trap: Jayarāśi Bhaṭṭa's Tattvopaplavasiṃha goes further, rejecting even perception, leading to radical skepticism.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Do not sacrifice this precious, fragile, living embodiment on the altar of unprovable otherworldly promises. Cherish life with honesty and courage here and now.

flashcards.topic: Metaphysics of Forms & The Divided Line
flashcards.concept_name: Plato: The Theory of Forms, Divided Line & Allegory of the Cave

chain.from_concept: Heraclitean Flux vs. Parmenidean Changeless Being
chain.current_thesis: Sensory things are imperfect shadows of eternal, immutable, intelligible archetypes (Forms / Ideai) accessible only to reason.
chain.to_concept: Aristotle's Hylomorphism (Grounding forms inside physical substances)

flashcards.the_problem: How can objective truth, knowledge, and moral ideals exist if everything in the sensory physical universe is constantly decaying and changing?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The transcendent, non-spatial, eternal essence of things (Justice, Beauty, Equality, The Good).
Four epistemic states: Eikasia (imagination), Pistis (belief), Dianoia (thought/math), Noesis (direct dialectical insight).
Sensory particulars exist by 'participating' in their transcendent Form.
Learning is not acquiring new data, but recollecting what the immortal soul knew before embodiment.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Sophists like Protagoras claimed 'Man is the measure of all things'—truth is subjective and relative to individual sensory impressions.
dialectic.siddhanta: Plato proves in the Republic and Phaedo: Two sticks are never perfectly equal; they strive toward the concept of Equality itself. We could not judge things as imperfect unless our intellect already possessed the perfect standard. The Form of the Good is the sun of the intelligible universe.

primary_text.author: Plato
primary_text.passage: Books VI & VII (The Sun, the Divided Line, and the Cave: 507b–518d)

flashcards.interview_trap: What is the 'Third Man Argument' against the Theory of Forms? (Posed by Plato himself in the Parmenides): If particulars resemble a Form, must there not be a third Form to account for the resemblance between the particulars and the Form, ad infinitum?
flashcards.wisdom_gist: We live chained to shadows on the wall of habit and convention. True education is the difficult, courageous ascent into the bright light of truth.

flashcards.concept_name: Aristotle: The Four Causes, Hylomorphism & Actuality/Potentiality

chain.from_concept: Plato's Transcendent Dual-World Theory of Forms
chain.current_thesis: Forms do not float in a separate heaven; they are immanent in matter (Hylomorphism), realizing potentiality into actuality.
chain.to_concept: Medieval Scholasticism (Aquinas's Five Ways & Essence-Existence)

flashcards.the_problem: How does natural change occur without creating reality out of nothing or freezing reality into Parmenidean immobility?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Every concrete substance (ousia) is an indissoluble composite of Matter (potency) and Form (actuality).
Material (bronze), Formal (statue shape), Efficient (sculptor), Final (telos/honor).
The acorn is potentially an oak tree; the mature oak tree is the realized actuality.
Nature does nothing in vain; every entity is pulled forward by its inherent purpose or natural goal.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Plato separated the Form from the concrete horse, creating an unbridgeable metaphysical chasm.
dialectic.siddhanta: Aristotle in Metaphysics Book VII argues: If forms exist separately, how do they cause change? Forms exist ONLY when instantiated in matter (except for the Unmoved Mover). Change is not impossible; change is the actualization of potentiality (energeia of dunamis).

primary_text.author: Aristotle
primary_text.passage: Physics II.3 (Four Causes); Metaphysics VII–IX (Substance and Actuality)

flashcards.interview_trap: What is 'Primary Substance' (Prōtē Ousia) for Aristotle in the Categories vs Metaphysics? In the Categories, primary substance is the individual concrete particular (this man, this horse); in Metaphysics VII, it is identified with the essential Form that makes the matter this specific thing.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Growth is not an arbitrary accident. Within every seed, every thought, and every human being lies a slumbering potential waiting to flower into its true form.

flashcards.concept_name: Aristotle: Eudaimonia, Aretē & The Doctrine of the Mean

chain.from_concept: Platonic Idea of the Transcendent Good & Hedonism
chain.current_thesis: The highest good is human flourishing (Eudaimonia) achieved through virtuous activity (Aretē) adhering to the Golden Mean.
chain.to_concept: Modern Virtue Ethics (MacIntyre & Foot) vs Deontology/Utilitarianism

flashcards.the_problem: What is the ultimate end (telos) of human action that is desired for its own sake and never as a means to something else?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Activity of the soul in accordance with complete virtue across a complete life.
The disposition of character that makes a human perform their unique function (ergon) well.
Virtue is the intermediate state between two vices: an excess and a deficiency.
The intellectual virtue that perceives the appropriate action, in the right way, for the right purpose.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Common men seek pleasure, politicians seek honor, and merchants seek wealth as the ultimate good of human life.
dialectic.siddhanta: Aristotle dismantles these in Book I of Nicomachean Ethics: Pleasure reduces us to grazing cattle; honor depends on others rather than ourselves; wealth is merely a means to buy things. The supreme good must fulfill the unique human function (ergon)—which is rational activity in accordance with virtue.

primary_text.author: Aristotle
primary_text.passage: Book I (The Function Argument: 1097a–1098b) & Book II (The Mean: 1106a–1107a)

flashcards.interview_trap: Is the Golden Mean a rigid mathematical midpoint? ABSOLUTELY NOT! Aristotle emphasizes it is the mean 'relative to us' (pros hēmas). What is courageous for a seasoned soldier may be rash for an untrained child; practical wisdom (phronesis) discerns the context.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Virtue is not a sporadic act or a burdensome rule; it is an enduring habit of excellence. We become just by practicing just actions, and courageous by practicing courage.

flashcards.concept_name: Spinoza: Substance Monism (Deus sive Natura) & Intellectual Love of God

chain.from_concept: Cartesian Mind-Body Dualism (The pineal gland interaction problem)
chain.current_thesis: There is only one infinite, eternal substance: God or Nature (Deus sive Natura); Mind and Matter are two of its infinite attributes.
chain.to_concept: Leibniz's Monadology (Recovering pluralism and individual agency)

flashcards.the_problem: How can mind and body interact if they are completely separate Cartesian substances with zero common properties?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Substance monism: God and the physical-mental universe are identical.
Nature as active creating cause (substance) vs Nature as passive manifested modes.
The fundamental striving of every entity to persevere in its own being.
Viewing events under the aspect of eternity, free from personal egoic bias.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Descartes posited two created substances (res cogitans and res extensa) needing God to mediate interaction in the brain.
dialectic.siddhanta: Spinoza proves geometrically in the Ethics: By definition, a substance is that which is conceived through itself and needs no other concept. Two distinct substances with different attributes cannot affect each other. Therefore, only ONE infinite substance can exist: God. Mind and Body are not two separate things, but two parallel expressions of the same reality.

primary_text.author: Baruch Spinoza
primary_text.passage: Part I (De Deo), Propositions 1–15 & Part V (On Human Freedom)

flashcards.interview_trap: Was Spinoza an atheist or a pantheist? Novalis called him 'a God-intoxicated man'! Spinoza rejected a transcendent personal creator who acts with human-like emotions or purposes; for Spinoza, teleology is human vanity projected onto the impersonal, beautiful necessity of Nature.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Freedom does not come from rebellious illusions of an uncaused free will, but from understanding the magnificent necessity of the cosmos and aligning our hearts with the whole.

flashcards.concept_name: Frege: Sense (Sinn) & Reference (Bedeutung)

chain.from_concept: Locke's Ideational Theory of Meaning (Words refer to private ideas)
chain.current_thesis: Meaning splits into the mode of presentation (Sense/Sinn) and the actual worldly object or truth-value (Reference/Bedeutung).
chain.to_concept: Russell's Theory of Definite Descriptions (On Denoting)

flashcards.the_problem: How can an identity statement like 'The Morning Star is the Evening Star' be an informative discovery, while 'The Morning Star is the Morning Star' is a boring tautology?

technical_lexicon.meaning: The objective cognitive mode of presentation (Art des Gegebenseins) contained within an expression.
The actual object picked out in the world, or the truth-value (True or False) of a sentence.
Never ask for the meaning of a word in isolation, but only in the context of a proposition.
Sentences containing non-referring terms have a sense but lack a truth-value for Frege.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Mill claimed names are mere tags with denotation but no connotation. If 'Morning Star' and 'Evening Star' just denote the planet Venus, then 'a = b' says nothing more than 'a = a'.
dialectic.siddhanta: Frege proves in 1892: 'Morning Star' and 'Evening Star' have the IDENTICAL Bedeutung (Venus), but totally DIFFERENT senses (Sinn). Identity statements expand knowledge when they inform us that two different modes of presentation pick out the same worldly object.

primary_text.author: Gottlob Frege
primary_text.work: On Sense and Reference (Über Sinn und Bedeutung)
primary_text.passage: Zeitschrift für Philosophie und philosophische Kritik (1892): 25–50

flashcards.interview_trap: What is the reference of a declarative sentence for Frege? The TRUTH-VALUE (The True or The False)! The sense of a sentence is the PROPOSITION or Thought (Gedanke). This is a standard UGC NET / Central University test question.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Words are not transparent glass. How we present a truth shapes what we understand. Two paths may lead to the same mountain, yet reveal completely different landscapes along the journey.

flashcards.concept_name: Kant: The Categorical Imperative & Kingdom of Ends

chain.from_concept: Utilitarianism & Moral Sentimentalism (Hume: Reason is slave of passions)
chain.current_thesis: Morality is grounded in pure practical reason; act only on maxims that can be willed as universal laws, treating persons as ends.
chain.to_concept: Hegel's Critique of Kantian Moral Rigorism (Sittlichkeit vs Moralität)

flashcards.the_problem: Can moral duty hold unconditional necessity if moral rules depend on human desires, consequences, or emotional inclinations?

technical_lexicon.meaning: Unconditional duty ('Do X!') vs Conditional prudence ('If you want Y, do X').
Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.
Act in such a way that you treat humanity, whether in your own person or another, always as an end and never merely as a means.
The moral agent is both author and subject of the moral law, free from heteronomous desires.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Utilitarians argue: An act is good because of its beneficial consequences; lying to save an innocent life produces net happiness.
dialectic.siddhanta: Kant insists in the Groundwork: Only a GOOD WILL is good without qualification. If everyone made lying promises when in trouble, the very institution of promising would logically self-destruct (contradiction in conception). Moral worth lies in duty for duty's sake, not consequences.

primary_text.author: Immanuel Kant
primary_text.work: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals

flashcards.interview_trap: Distinguish 'Perfect Duties' from 'Imperfect Duties' in Kant: Perfect duties (do not lie, do not commit suicide) result in a 'contradiction in CONCEPTION' if universalized; Imperfect duties (cultivate talents, help others) result in a 'contradiction in the WILL'.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: Human beings possess dignity, not a price. To treat another human being as a mere tool for our own convenience is to betray the sacred light of reason within ourselves.

flashcards.concept_name: John Rawls: Justice as Fairness & The Veil of Ignorance

chain.from_concept: Classical Utilitarianism (Sacrificing minority rights for aggregate happiness)
chain.current_thesis: Principles of justice are those that free and rational persons would agree to in an initial position of equality behind a Veil of Ignorance.
chain.to_concept: Robert Nozick's Libertarian Entitlement Theory & Sen's Capabilities Approach

flashcards.the_problem: How can a democratic society construct fair, non-arbitrary terms of social cooperation among citizens divided by conflicting religious and philosophical doctrines?

technical_lexicon.meaning: A hypothetical thought experiment of pure procedural fairness ensuring impartial agreement.
Parties know nothing of their own class, race, gender, intelligence, or conception of the good.
Each person has an equal right to the most extensive system of equal basic liberties.
Social and economic inequalities are permissible ONLY if they work to the greatest benefit of the least-advantaged.

dialectic.purvapaksha: Utilitarians argue that social arrangements should maximize the total or average well-being of the majority, even if some suffer.
dialectic.siddhanta: Rawls opens A Theory of Justice: 'Justice is the first virtue of social institutions, as truth is of systems of thought.' Each person possesses an inviolability founded on justice that even the welfare of society cannot override. Behind the veil, rational agents choose the MAXIMIN rule—protecting the worst-off position.

flashcards.interview_trap: What is the 'Lexical Priority' (lexicographical order) in Rawls? The First Principle (Equal Liberty) has absolute priority over the Second Principle! You cannot trade away fundamental civil and political liberties for economic gains.
flashcards.wisdom_gist: A just society is measured not by the luxury of its billionaires or the grandeur of its monuments, but by the dignity and security it guarantees to its most vulnerable citizens.
